hero.lede: Solon runs governance for companies, towns, associations and communities — proposals, votes and the books, where every member can see them.

glarus.title: The whole town. One square. Every hand counted.
glarus.body: Since at least 1387 the citizens of Glarus have met in their town square to make their own laws. Anyone may speak; anyone may propose a change. In 2006 one citizen's amendment from the floor merged twenty-five municipalities into three. Solon brings that to any group — at any size, from anywhere.
glarus.cta: The art and science of governance

propose.title: Propose
propose.body: Anyone with a seat puts a question on the record, in plain words, with exactly what would change.

decide.title: Decide
decide.body: Members vote with one click, under rules the group chose: who votes, how votes are counted, how many must agree.

carryOut.title: Carry out
carryOut.body: The result is published with every vote behind it — so everyone knows what was decided, and can hold the people carrying it out to it.

rules.title: Same people. Different rules. Different winner.
rules.body: Seven members, one shared fund, four ways to spend it. Change only how the question is asked and watch the winner change. Nothing here is a mock-up — it runs the same counting code as a real vote.

agent.title: Works for all of you. Never for one of you.
agent.body: Every group has more to keep track of than anyone has time for. Solon's governance agent does the clerk's work — in the open, under the same rules as everyone else.
agent.note: It proposes and reminds; people decide. Some decisions — who may join, and the rules themselves — only people can vote on. Being built with our first pilot groups.

writes.title: Writes it up
writes.body: Turns a request in plain words into a clear proposal that says exactly what would change.

informs.title: Keeps everyone in the loop
informs.body: Tells members what is up for decision, reminds them before a vote closes, and keeps the minutes.

money.title: Follows the money
money.body: Checks what was spent against what was decided, and raises anything nobody voted for.

explains.title: Explains, never persuades
explains.body: Sets out the case for and against every proposal, and explains every result in plain language.

companies.title: Companies
companies.body: Board and shareholder decisions, with a record nobody can quietly edit.

towns.title: Villages and towns
towns.body: Assemblies, budgets and local rules — open to every resident, wherever they are.

associations.title: Associations and co-ops
associations.body: General meetings, elections and member votes, minuted as they happen.

communities.title: Communities and new towns
communities.body: Groups online and new kinds of towns that want to govern themselves from day one.

record.title: Every vote on the record
record.body: Members see every proposal, every vote and how it was counted.

grows.title: A record that only grows
grows.body: Nothing on the record can be edited or deleted — not even by us.

money.title: We never hold your money
money.body: Solon watches the accounts you register and shows where money went. It cannot spend.

proof.title: Proof when you need it
proof.body: Members can sign their votes with their own key, so anyone can recount them without trusting Solon.

hire.title: We'll run your governance with you.
hire.body: Tell us about your group. We set up your rules together, run your first decisions, and keep the record. Free for pilot groups while Solon is in beta.

Hire.metaTitle: Hire Solon — governance, run with you
Hire.metaDescription: Solon sets up your group's rules with you, runs your decisions and keeps the record — for companies, towns, associations and communities.

hero.title: Governance, run with you.
hero.lede: You decide. We make sure every decision is asked clearly, counted fairly, and kept on a record your members can trust.

rules.title: Your rules, written down
rules.body: We work out with you how your group decides today — who votes, on what, how many must agree — and set it up so everyone can read it and change it by vote.

decisions.title: Decisions, run end to end
decisions.body: Proposals, votes, reminders and minutes, for meetings in a room, online, or both. Members vote with one click from wherever they are.

agent.title: The governance agent
agent.body: Drafts proposals from plain requests, keeps members informed, and checks what was spent against what was decided. It never takes a side, and never decides.

person.title: A person when it matters
person.body: A facilitator who knows how groups decide — for the founding meeting, the difficult vote, and the disagreement nobody wants to have.

suits.title: From a board of five to a town of thousands.

companies.title: Companies
companies.body: Board resolutions, shareholder votes and policies, on a record nobody can quietly edit.

towns.title: Villages and towns
towns.body: Assemblies, budgets and local rules, open to every resident — in the hall and from home.

associations.title: Associations and co-ops
associations.body: General meetings, elections and member votes, with the minutes written as it happens.

communities.title: Communities and new towns
communities.body: Online groups and new kinds of towns that want fair rules and an open record from the start.

start.title: Three conversations, then your first decision.

tell.title: Tell us
tell.body: Who your group is, how it decides today, and what goes wrong. Half an hour, no forms.

write.title: Write the rules
write.body: We draft your rules together — plainly enough that every member can read them.

decide.title: Decide
decide.body: Your first real decision runs on Solon, with us alongside. After that, it is yours.

cost.title: What it costs
cost.body: Nothing, for pilot groups, while Solon is in beta. You get the full service; we learn what your group needs and build it. When pricing exists, it will be on this page before anyone is asked to pay it.
cost.own: Or start an organization on your own — it takes a minute

Security.metaDescription: Why Solon can be trusted with a group's decisions: what it refuses to hold, and what anyone can check.
Security.title: What we refuse to hold
Security.lede: Solon's security comes from what it cannot do: it holds no money, keeps no one's keys, and cannot rewrite what happened.

money.title: We never hold your money
money.body: Solon watches the accounts a group registers and shows where money went. There is no code path that can spend.
money.d1: A treasury is an address to observe — a label and an address, nothing more
money.d2: Balances are read from the public chain, not from Solon's own numbers

keys.title: We never hold anyone's keys
keys.body: Nothing on Solon's servers lets an attacker vote as someone else with a signature, or move a single coin.
keys.d1: Members who sign keep their key in their own wallet
keys.d2: Agent members (the Cat, Loki) sign on their own machines — Solon only ever sees signatures

proof.title: Every vote says what proves it
proof.body: A member votes with one click while signed in, or signs with their own key. Every vote and proposal records which.
proof.d1: A one-click vote is Solon's record of a signed-in member's choice — convenient, and it asks you to trust Solon
proof.d2: A signed vote is accepted only if it matches the member's registered key, and anyone can re-check it
proof.d3: One ballot per member per vote; voting again replaces it until the vote closes

record.title: The record only grows
record.body: Every step — a proposal, a vote opening, each ballot, the result — is written once. Nothing in the code can edit or delete it.
record.d1: The public record shows the entries themselves, not a summary of them
record.d2: The rules a vote ran under are frozen when it opens, so a later change cannot rewrite a past decision
record.d3: Every decision is published as one document with everything needed to recount it

seize.title: Nothing to seize
seize.body: Breaking into Solon's servers yields no keys and no money — only records that were already public.

forge.title: Nothing to forge
forge.body: A signed vote cannot be faked by anyone, Solon included. Groups that want that guarantee for a decision can ask members to sign.

rewrite.title: Nothing to rewrite
rewrite.body: A decision travels with its evidence. Anyone relying on it can recount it themselves — Solon's word is evidence, not authority.
